newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opposition says PRI waging dirty campaign.
newsitem.headline: Mexico opposition says PRI waging dirty campaign.

text.p: Mexican opposition parties on Sunday accused the government of waging a dirty campaign against them in towns that recently voted for the opposition, raising tensions ahead of key mid-term elections in July.

Members of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) have in the past weeks clashed with police in scores of towns across Mexico that recently voted against the PRI and are now under opposition control.
On Friday, pro-PRI supporters clashed with police in three separate towns run by the opposition. At least 27 people were injured in the scuffles, police said.
"The ruling party is running scared and resorting to aggressive tactics," said Felipe Calderon, head of the conservative National Action Party (PAN).
"It's the politics of gangsterism," Manuel Lopez Obrador, head of the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) was quoted as saying in Reforma newspaper on Sunday.
No one was available for comment on the charges at the Mexico City headquarters of the PRI.
Opposition leaders said the dirty tactics followed much tougher talking recently taken by President Ernesto Zedillo and new PRI leader Humberto Roque Villanueva.
Zedillo recently criticised the international press for portraying Mexico, which has been ruled by the PRI for 67 years, as a one-party state.
And Villanueva, who has been at the PRI's helm for only a few months, recently attacked the PRD as a party that would lead to "dictatorship" and the PAN as "fascist."
Mexicans go to the polls in July to elect a new congress and, for the first time ever, a mayor for Mexico City.
The PAN and, more recently, the PRD have won a string of victories in recent local elections as support for the long-ruling PRI has eroded after a recent economic crisis and corruption scandals.
